title: Improve Project Configuration Files Format

milestone.title: 0.0.0.9500 Standardized API data columns
milestone.description: Different data sources call the same thing different things. The codebase originally did not have overlap, but currently the overlap leads to lack of clarity. Some functions also evolved: For example, parse_*_network() now has an alternative function parse_*_temporal_network(). Therefore parse_*_network() should be renamed to parse_*_bipartite_network() or renamed altogether. See #43.

body:
Now that newer data sources and tools are available in Kaiaulu, the project configuration file sections are becoming more confusing. There is also little comment guidance on what is needed or not, or what is part of Kaiaulu or what is not. 

The overall format should be refactored to facilitate understand its purpose, where to obtain the field values and what uses them. 

Fundamentally, these files take inspiration from Codeface, but go a bit further. The goal is to "distill" a project's website available infrastructure information, and therefore data, in a concise, reusable file that can be manually checked and reused for other analysis. For instance, here is a list of questions that often wastes manual time to be answered for every analyzed project:

 1.  Version Control:
    1. What version control system is used? Git, SVN, something else? 
    2. Where is the data for analysis X? 
 2. Mailing List: 
    1. What mailing list archives the project use? (e.g. pipermail, mod_mbox, MARC, google groups, etc)
       1. Do they contain the same data? (OpenSSL is a classic example where each archive contains a portion of the full mailing list!)  
    2. What mailing list should be used for analysis? Developer and User, or just developer? Any other mailing list?
    3. What is the URL for the mailing lists we should use?
    4. Where is the data for analysis X? 
 3. Issue Tracker
    1. What issue tracker type is used (BugZilla, JIRA, GitHub, TRAC, etc)
    2. Where is the data for analysis X?
4. Files 
    1. What language does the project use? (Needed as a parameter for static analysis tools, and to avoid including non src code files in your churn metrics!)
    2. How do developers convention test files? (Need to also avoid bloating churn and other content metrics)
    3. Do commit messages contain conventions for issues or software vulnerabilities? (Needed for bug count metric, or software vulnerability analysis). 
  
These questions all require some manual time is spent googling the project website to find (which is not even always easy to locate), manual inspection of commit messages to curate a regular expression, etc. A project configuration file should make it easier for a person to quickly assess that, and more importantly, stop wasting time searching for it. This information is of course not immutable: An analysis of OpenSSL over its entire 20 years lifespan shown it started with mailing lists, overlapped with a bug tracker and mailing list, and eventually moved fully to GitHub. So some minimal validation the links in the files are current, or sufficient for the analysis of interest, is still important.

Of course, the information in this file can be capitalized by Kaiaulu to do something: Knowing the online source of a VCS, Mailing list or issue tracker can be used by a crawler to obtain the data, whereas the local path can be used to execute the pipeline in the R Notebooks, and eventually via a command-line interface.

# Analysis 

From here, the second concern is reproducibility in MSR and the analysis, which is often buried in online folders, or e-mails. For example, was only a portion of the project X mailing list used? What was the time window? What commits range was used in the git log? Or what types of file dependencies were used? These parameters are per analysis, but missing one of them dooms any future attempt to effectively compare results. These parameters have to nonetheless be decided so an analysis can occur, and deferred to the user instead of hardcoded and buried under functions, which is unlikely to be found on normal usage of the tool. Further thought on whether embed this on a project configuration file or R Notebook directly is still needed.

title: Social smell identity match is currently done on slice instead of full dataset
body:
@CorneJB 

> One of the challenges is that identity_match() happens on the slice level and this results in non-congruent identity_id's across slices. Using the mail-adresses and names in the slices introduces the noise that identity_match() normally solves. This could maybe be solved by applying identity_match() outside of the loop on the whole gitlog (probably incurring a performance hit) or using the start/end commit to define where it is applied.

Actually, the identity_match() should work on either, since the git log slice is in essence a git log table with fewer rows. In Kaiaulu 0.0.0.9000 it used to be applied only after a transform_* function, which led to the issue you noted for doing this inside a loop:


https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/2486a1a5d775e1338de20980266c67b52df23db3/vignettes/social_smells_showcase.Rmd#L222-L227

so I removed that requirement to be a network in 0.0.0.9500. Could you try applying it to the entire gitlog and mailing list as output from parse_gitlog and parse_mbox at the start of the following notebook as shown here but with also the mbox?

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/71dae8b29851453d58d85cdf331f42f79d9145e3/vignettes/gitlog_showcase.Rmd#L102-L114

In other words instead of inside the loop:

```r
  project_log <- list(project_git_slice=project_git_slice,project_mbox_slice=project_mbox_slice)
  project_log <- identity_match(project_log,
                                name_column = c("author_name_email","reply_from"),
                                assign_exact_identity,
                                use_name_only=TRUE,
                                label = "raw_name"
                                )
```

do:

```r
  project_log <- list(project_git=project_git,project_mbox=project_mbox)
  project_log <- identity_match(project_log,
                                name_column = c("author_name_email","reply_from"),
                                assign_exact_identity,
                                use_name_only=TRUE,
                                label = "raw_name"

  project_git <- project_log[["project_git"]]
  project_mbox <- project_log[["project_mbox"]]
```

outside the loop, and remove the associated step from inside the loops. I will update the Notebook once I have the chance. Thanks for catching this!

title: Adding developer turnover metrics to smells notebook
body:
Hi!

I made this today for analyzing the turnover between analysis windows based on the quality metrics in Magnoni (2016)'s dissertation. I did not really know where to put it in terms of branches, issues, and pulls, so I'm dropping it here to get some feedback and create a branch/pull if it is needed/wanted. The for-loop below uses  `project_git_slicestack`, which is a list containing the slices that are made during the social smells part of the social smells showcase vignette. 

```
## Initiate turnover variable
code_dev_turnover <- list()

## Loop through slices and calculate turnover based on Magnoni (2016)
for(i in 1:length(project_git_slicestack)){
  
  ## Calculate developer turnover between slices and add to smells table
  if(i != 1){
    
    x1 <- unique(project_git_slicestack[[i - 1]]$author_name_email)
    x2 <- unique(project_git_slicestack[[i]]$author_name_email)
  
    neldy <- length(setdiff(x1,x2))
    neby <- length(x1)
    neey <- length(x2)
  
    code_dev_turnover[i] <- signif((neldy / ((neby + neey)/2)), digits = 3)
    
    smells[[i]]$code_dev_turnover <- code_dev_turnover[i]
    
  } else { ## Don't calculate for the fist window and add to smells table
    
    code_dev_turnover[i] <- "NULL"
    
    smells[[i]]$code_dev_turnover <- code_dev_turnover[i]
    
  }
```

Kind regards,

Corné Broere

title: Networks in Kaiaulu and 3rd party dependencies

labels.name: priority:future
labels.description: For issues which will be deferred / wishlist

labels.name: module:graph
labels.description: Issues related to the graph module

body:
Currently, Kaiaulu has a really ad-hoc implementation of [networks](https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/master/R/network.R) (i.e. it represents in a list nodes and edges tables, each being a data.table). The definition grew organically to use the visualizations provided by vizNetwork for exploration early on, but it doesn't make sense to, from here onwards, re-code an entire network library. 

In Codeface4Smells, the Smells were built on top of igraph and leverages its bipartite projection algorithms. However, doing so here would automatically re-license the codebase from MPL 2.0 to GPL. Moreover, it is hard to believe igraph is the only library available out there.

This issue is a small survey of existing tools found "in the wild" for consideration, not only based on the license but on features, etc, and for reflection on how far we need to go in regards to dependencies. Generally, I would prefer to not consider such a core data model and functionality of the package dependent on anything (unless it is incorporated directly to the codebase and doesn't cost setup overhead).

title: Different timezone in Ubuntu leads to data.AuthorDate being NA in parse_gitlog()
body:
Bug found by @massihonda 

Quoting e-mail exchange:

# Problem

> In the script gitlog_showcases.Rmd, the function parse_gitlog should create a dataframe with a column that records the date of the commits (data.AuthorDate). However, in my environment this column is filled with NA. So, in the part project_git_slice it does not select any raw, because none of them have a date.

>  After inserting the line Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "C"), the timestamps were correctly assessed and the scripts ran properly.

> The problem was in the function as.POSIXct, because I think the date format in my laptop did not match (my date is by default in italian format). The command Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "C") changes the format in my laptop to the english format. (source: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/45565986/as-posixlt-returns-na).. The parameter "C" is OS dependent, in Windows I think it is "English".

Current file filter allows for the config file to specify for a given project:

title: reimplement parse_gitlog() to use git log command to handle 20GB+ git logs

labels.name: module:collaboration_network
labels.description: Issues related to collaboration network construction, parsing and metrics.

body:
While this may seem like a reverse from #33, I have observed git log interfaces allow for grep filtering the commit messages ([and even the source code down the road if we so decide](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/22055390/how-to-install-git-with-pcre-support-on-osx-with-homebrew)), while perceval interface will not afford me the luxury.

This functionality is very important for the analysis of massive project git logs like Chromium, which have 20GB of data when our interest is on very specific commits. The filtering from raw is much faster, and most importantly, avoid choking R by trying to pass a 20GB blob on memory to then parse the data. 
 
If we want to only get the git log containing certain bug ids from Chromium, we can have git log do that for us like so: 

`git log --no-merges master --grep="(?i)bug=119250|bug=117627" --perl-regexp`

This specifies we do not want merge commits, that we want to look only on the master branch, and the regular expression to apply. `(?i)` [will make the word bug case insensitive to match](https://regular-expressions.mobi/modifiers.html?wlr=1). 

Using the option `--perl-regexp` is important, otherwise, git log will not understand `|` as OR operator. The example above applied to chromium returned nothing without using it. When using `--perl-regexp` one problem I encountered was the following error on OS X Catalina 10.15.1:

```
cannot use Perl-compatible regexes when not compiled with USE_LIBPCRE
```

The following stackoverflow suggested [upgrading via brew](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/22055390/how-to-install-git-with-pcre-support-on-osx-with-homebrew). I noticed my installation was from elsewhere under version `git version 2.23.0`. 

Brew installation as of this date is `git 2.27.0`. Simply installing the current brew git, and accepting it's suggestion to overwrite the existing git symlinks:

```
==> Installing git
==> Pouring git-2.27.0.catalina.bottle.tar.gz
Error: The `brew link` step did not complete successfully
The formula built, but is not symlinked into /usr/local
Could not symlink bin/git
Target /usr/local/bin/git
already exists. You may want to remove it:
  rm '/usr/local/bin/git'

To force the link and overwrite all conflicting files:
  brew link --overwrite git

To list all files that would be deleted:
  brew link --overwrite --dry-run git
```

Sufficed to enable the --perl-regexp. 

With these changes in place, and git enabled to use compatible regular expressions, Kaiaulu can them leverage this new interface to sub-set Chromium's 20GB log into very few megabytes, and use Perceval or any other git log parser to parse as json the much smaller dataset.

title: Leverage Perceval time window parsing of git logs on parse_gitlog() interface

labels.name: module:collaboration_network
labels.description: Issues related to collaboration network construction, parsing and metrics.

body:
Perceval `git` interface provides the following parameters:

```
  --from-date FROM_DATE
                        fetch items updated since this date (in any ISO 8601
                        format, e.g., 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:SS +|-HH:MM')
  --to-date TO_DATE     fetch items updated before this date (in any ISO 8601
                        format, e.g., 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:SS +|-HH:MM')
```

parse_gitlog() can have two additional parameters to specify the time range. Unfortunately, the interface does not provide intervals by commit hash, but this may (I hope) save computation time for quick exploration on large projects.

body:
[Who is Who in the Mailing List? Comparing Six Disambiguation Heuristics to Identify Multiple Addresses of a Participant
](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/7816480) provides a comparison of different ways to approach this problem. 

As of the publication of the article, the most cited was [Bird's 2006 mining e-mail social networks](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/bird2006mes.pdf). 

This python package provides different distance metrics: [jellyfish](https://github.com/jamesturk/jellyfish). But in the interest of keeping the number of dependencies to a minimum, we can try to implement them on as a need-basis.

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/7ee45d3861714e4fa93a2e17af203d7570b55031/vignettes/depends_showcase.Rmd#L64-L72

## Java 

Suggestion by Humberto Cervantes: 

 * Projects analyses should not include test files
 * Exclude files that have “test” on the package
 * Exclude files that have “example”, or “sample” in the path
 * Exclude generated source code

 * And they also exclude anything that is not source code.  In their case that is .java files.  In our case we can enumerate the languages. It's not a large set (e.g. .java, .cc, .c, .h, etc.) and exclude other files.

# Other Languages

We would also need to create regex for at least Java, Python, C, and C++, all of which are supported by Depends.

title: Removal of .git, .mbox can accidentally remove other parts of the path
body:
# Input 

```r
stri_split_regex("/Users/cvp/Desktop/kaiaulu_project_input/git_repos/Cassandra/.git",".git")
```

# Output

```
[[1]]
[1] "/Users/cvp/Desktop/kaiaulu_project_input" "_repos/Cassandra/"                       
[3] ""    
```

This occurs on R/parser.R functions. Using `stri_replace_last` addresses the problem and is correctly used in `parse_dependencies()`. Needs to be applied on the other `parse_` functions.
